topic.title: What if every billionaire's money on Forbes' 2026 list were shared out to everyone on Earth?

title: Elon Musk and every billionaire, shared with you: how much each? 💸
description:
What if Elon Musk's money, and every other billionaire's, were shared out to every person alive: how much would land in your hand?
Sources: Forbes World's Billionaires 2026, US Census Bureau (Jul 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Your share once, or the billionaires keep it? Comment

lines.text: Split Elon Musk's money, and every billionaire's, with everyone. Your cut?
Together they own $20.1T, and Forbes counts only 3,428 of them.
Musk alone owns $839B. That's 4.2% of the whole pile.
Now split it over 8.2B people. What does each one get?
Musk's part alone gives each person about $102.
So everyone gets rich? Not even close.
Each of us gets about $2,451, once. Then the pile is gone.
One cheque each, or their whole pile: which would you pick? So

Re-review of the changed promise line 'Together they own $20.1T, and Forbes counts only 3,428 of them.': same facts (fact1 $20.1T, fact2 3,428), credited to Forbes and confirmed earlier (forbes.com 403; confirmed by search in Scripps News, Spokesman-Review/Yahoo Finance, The Standard HK, City AM and the BusinessWire copy of Forbes' release: a record 3,428 billionaires worth $20.1T on the 2026 list, 1 Mar 2026 prices). The picture (scoreboard total, then the count) matches the words. Style note: 'counts only 3,428 of them' could be heard as Forbes missing some; 'and there are only 3,428 of them on Forbes' list' would be clearer. Earlier note stands: Musk is $869B on Forbes' 1 Nov 2026 estimate, so 'on Forbes' 2026 list' would make the Musk line exact. No advice, disclaimer present.

Your cut?') is a question with no figure and no claim; its picture (empty cup, YOUR CUT? tag) matches it. The Musk beat (fact3 $839B, muskpct 4.2%) uses unchanged facts and maths. Facts were confirmed earlier: Census page shows 8.2B for Jul 2026; forbes.com 403, so 3,428 / $20.1T / Musk $839B on Forbes' 2026 list (1 Mar 2026 prices) were confirmed by search in Scripps News, Spokesman-Review/Yahoo Finance, The Standard HK, City AM and the BusinessWire copy of Forbes' release. Still true: Forbes' 1 Nov 2026 estimate has Musk at $869B, so 'on Forbes' 2026 list' in the Musk line would be more exact. No advice, disclaimer present.

[script] 9.6-14.7 s, beat 'musk' (Quarry.tsx; stills 10.5/12.0/13.5 s): not directed like the reference. There is no place, only plain blue sky over a brown floor behind a coin pyramid, a bare line and a yellow pole (no quarry, no crane). Nobody acts for the whole 5 s beat. The 'gap' cut into the mountain is a dark brown quad that sticks out past the pyramid's right slope, a drawing bug. Build a real quarry with a crane and an operator or Rohan, make the lifted slab visibly about 4% of the mountain, and clip the gap to the pile.

[script] 4.0-6.5 s, beat 'promise': the second sentence is 'Forbes counts 3,428 billionaires.', a count or setup in the 5 s window. This repeats lessons.md #3 and #4 (the second sentence must be a bigger surprise, never a setup or a count). Lead with the surprise, e.g. the $20.1T pile, and put the 3,428 count after it as the contrast.

[script] 29.5-33 s, beat 'loop' (Loop.tsx; stills 30.0/31.5/32.9 s): Rohan's cheque, the thing the line names ('One cheque each'), is drawn behind his head and only a pale sliver shows. Hold it out to the side, in front of him, with the $2,451 readable so the pick-one has both choices on screen.
